sources.name: National Lottery Community Fund: all funding programmes
National Lottery Community Fund: Awards for All England

grants.title: National Lottery Awards for All England
grants.summary: Grants of £300 to £20,000 for projects that bring people together, build strong relationships and improve communities in England. Projects can last up to 2 years.
grants.body: The fund supports projects that bring people together to build strong relationships in and across communities, improve the places and spaces that matter to communities, help people reach their potential at the earliest stage, and support people and organisations facing extra pressures such as the cost of living. Groups can use the funding to start a new activity or continue an existing one, and to help their organisation adapt to new challenges. Projects may last up to 2 years. Projects focused on the environment are covered by a separate programme called National Lottery Awards for All England: Environment.

sources.name: National Lottery Community Fund: Awards for All England, Environment

grants.title: National Lottery Awards for All England – Environment
grants.summary: Funds community-led projects that improve the environment or help people connect with and care for nature. Grants from £300 to £20,000 for projects in England.
grants.body: The fund supports community-led projects that improve the environment and help people connect with and enjoy nature where they live. Projects must meet one of two priorities: helping people connect with and care for nature in their area, or making a positive difference to the environment. The money can be used to start a new activity or continue an existing one, help an organisation adapt to new challenges, or run one-off events with a clear environmental benefit. Organisations cannot apply if they already hold an Awards for All grant.
grants.eligibility: Open to community groups and voluntary organisations in England. Organisations that already have an Awards for All grant cannot apply.

sources.name: National Lottery Community Fund: Reaching Communities England

grants.title: Reaching Communities England
grants.summary: Funds projects that help strengthen communities and improve lives across England, with priority for places, people and communities facing poverty, disadvantage or discrimination. Grants range from £20,001 to £1,000,000 for projects of up to 5 years.
grants.body: The fund supports projects that help achieve one of four missions: bringing communities together through inclusive places and activities, helping children and young people thrive through positive social and emotional skills, tackling health inequalities by addressing the conditions in which people live, work and grow, and making communities environmentally sustainable. The funder is most likely to fund projects that support places, people or communities experiencing poverty, disadvantage or discrimination, and projects that support people and communities to shape the decisions that affect their lives. Most awards are under £500,000, and requests over £500,000 should be discussed with the funder first. Projects can last up to 5 years.

sources.name: National Lottery Community Fund: The UK Fund

grants.title: The UK Fund
grants.summary: Larger grants of £500,000 to £5,000,000 for established community work that shows proven impact and is ready to scale across the UK. Projects must meet one of five stated aims.
grants.body: The UK Fund supports work that is already making a difference and needs larger funding to grow. Applicants must show what is working, how they know it has a proven impact, and why the work is ready to scale. New projects or services that are brand new are not funded. Projects should go beyond delivering a service and help change how systems work, leading to lasting benefits for communities. The work should benefit communities across the UK, for example by working in different places or sharing learning between countries. Projects must meet one of the stated aims, including improving relationships between people with different life experiences, helping people connect online, supporting people to influence their communities, and helping children and young people change the systems that affect them. The funder particularly welcomes projects led by and for disabled people.

sources.name: National Lottery Community Fund: Climate Action Fund, Food Systems

grants.title: Climate Action Fund - Food Systems
grants.summary: Funds projects that strengthen the food system, reduce food insecurity and make a lasting impact on climate and nature through partnership working. Awards range from £2,500,000 to £7,000,000 over several years.
grants.body: The fund supports community organisations to grow and produce food using agroecological methods, to distribute food so that people have fair access to healthy, affordable food, and to offer people different food options, especially those facing poverty, disadvantage or discrimination. Projects must work towards systems change, addressing the root causes of food insecurity rather than only its symptoms. Applicants must show they will work in a partnership, make a lasting impact on climate change, the environment and nature, significantly increase access to healthy, affordable food, and plan to measure and share the impact of their work. Projects must also show how communities and organisations representing them will be meaningfully involved. Up to 10 projects are expected to be funded in the first year.

grants.title: National Lottery Heritage Grants £10,000 to £250,000
grants.summary: Funds heritage projects across the UK, from £10,000 up to £250,000. Covers any type of heritage that people value and want to pass on to future generations.
grants.body: This programme funds all types of heritage projects in the UK, including applications for the Fund's strategic initiatives. Heritage can be anything from the past that people value and want to pass on. Grants range from £10,000 to £250,000, with larger projects of up to £10 million handled through a separate programme. Check whether your project idea is suitable before applying.

grants.title: Movement Fund
grants.summary: Grants of up to £15,000 for physical activity projects in the community, focused on people who face barriers to being active.
grants.body: The Movement Fund supports community physical activity projects designed to help people who face barriers to taking part in activity. Sport England says it prioritises projects that give opportunities to groups who have not had as many chances to be active, including people on low incomes, disabled people and those with long-term health conditions, older people, people from culturally diverse communities, pregnant women and parents of very young children, girls aged 5 to 16, LGBTQ+ people, people in foster care and unpaid carers. Sport England also gives priority to projects in communities with greater need, using its Place Needs Classification and the Inequalities Metric. Projects that address several combined barriers, such as people with long-term health conditions who also have caring responsibilities, are of particular interest. Sport England receives more applications than it can fund, so projects are prioritised against its goal of getting more people active and tackling long-standing inequalities.

grants.body: The Football Foundation lists the Lionesses HERe to Play Fund among its funding programmes. The programme page is the place to check what it covers.

grants.body: The Football Foundation lists Goalposts as one of its funded items for grassroots football facilities. Football facilities must be available for community use. Kit and equipment are not covered by the sports grants.

grants.title: Premier League Stadium Fund
grants.summary: Football Foundation fund listed as the Premier League Stadium Fund.
grants.body: The Premier League Stadium Fund is listed by the Football Foundation as one of its funds. It has its own website, which sets out what it covers.

grants.title: The Future Places Fund
grants.summary: Fixed grants of £20,000 (£10,000 a year over two years) for creative community-led projects that shape the future of places in Leeds. Delivered with Leeds Civic Trust.
grants.body: The Future Places Fund invites communities across Leeds to come together and reimagine the future of the places they care about most. It supports creative community-led projects that give people a real voice in shaping their future and produce ideas and tangible outputs that can spark action, influence decisions and leave a lasting legacy. The grant is a fixed £20,000, paid as £10,000 a year over a two-year project. Decisions are expected in March 2027.
grants.eligibility: Community-led projects in Leeds. Applicants should be able to show that the project is led by the community.
grants.how_to_apply: Apply through the Future Places Fund page on the Leeds Community Foundation website before the closing date.

grants.title: Understanding Gambling Harm in Minority Ethnic Communities Fund
grants.summary: A pilot fund, run with Leeds City Council, for activities that improve understanding of gambling-related harm in Leeds minority ethnic communities and strengthen support pathways.
grants.body: This pilot fund is delivered in partnership with Leeds City Council to better understand gambling-related harm in Leeds minority ethnic communities. It supports activities that improve understanding of gambling patterns and related harms, reduce stigma, build community awareness and strengthen pathways to support. The fund is listed as an upcoming grant opening in December.

grants.title: Small Sparks Funding
grants.summary: Small grants of up to £500 for local groups and activities in Leeds that focus on preventing mental health problems and supporting wellbeing. Applications are open now.
grants.body: Small Sparks Funding offers small grants of up to £500 to local groups and activities that promote preventative mental health and wellbeing in Leeds. It can help start a new group, event or project, or keep an existing creative or community activity going. Applicants must show a clear description of how the money will be spent, with a breakdown of costs. The activity must take place in Leeds and must not already have Small Sparks funding for the same group or activity. Successful groups are asked to submit monitoring such as photos, quotes, an expenditure breakdown and a case study, attend one or two progress meetings with the Grants Coordinator, and use the Being You Leeds logo as project sponsor on promotional materials. Past projects supported include a men's group social, a long COVID art project, senior socials and a dance group.
grants.eligibility: Local groups and activities in Leeds focused on preventing mental health problems and supporting wellbeing. The applicant must be run by an unincorporated group or a not-for-profit organisation; profit-making organisations cannot apply. Groups that already receive public funding or support from Being You Leeds, Live Well Leeds, Better Together or Linking Leeds cannot apply, and nor can groups that already have Small Sparks funding for the same group or activity.
grants.how_to_apply: Email info@beingyouleeds.org.uk or speak to the Being You Leeds team on 0113 248 4880 to receive an application. The application must include a clear description of how the money will be spent and a breakdown of costs.

sources.name: Church Urban Fund: Windrush Day Grant Scheme

grants.title: Youth Joy Fund
grants.summary: Grants of £5,000 to £25,000 for organisations supporting LGBT+ young people aged 11 to 25 in England. Funds projects, trips and local events that build joy, belonging and wellbeing.
grants.body: The Youth Joy Fund is funded by The National Lottery Community Fund's You Decide programme and run by The LGBT+ Fund, powered by Consortium. It aims to help LGBT+ young people feel higher levels of self-acceptance, connection to community and wellbeing through youth work, community engagement, projects, trips and other enriching experiences. Applicants can ask for the amount they need within the £5,000 to £25,000 range. Priority is given to organisations in historically underfunded areas of the LGBT+ sector, areas lacking provision, and work supporting intersectional LGBT+ communities, such as LGBT+ young people with disabilities or from global majority backgrounds. Applications can be made online, by a short video of up to 5 minutes, or through a supported application by phone. Light-touch due diligence is followed by assessment from a community panel of LGBT+ people, with decisions expected by the end of March 2027.
grants.eligibility: Open to England based non-profit LGBT+ organisations or youth groups that currently support young people aged 11 to 25. Also open to non-profit youth organisations or groups that support LGBT+ young people aged 11 to 25 where the work is led by LGBT+ people, such as an LGBT+ youth group led by LGBT+ youth workers within a wider youth organisation. Organisations must have delivered youth work for at least 2 years and must have existing LGBT+ youth provision. Membership of Consortium is not required. Past grant recipients and current grant holders may apply.
grants.how_to_apply: Check eligibility with the eligibility checker and read the fund guidance before starting. Complete the online application form, or submit a short video of up to 5 minutes covering all written questions. A supported application by phone is available by contacting the Giving team early after the fund opens.

grants.title: Paddle Trust Funding Window
grants.summary: Grants to clubs, community groups and organisations across the UK to improve access to water and protect the environment. The funding window is open until 7th December 2026.
grants.body: The Paddle Trust funding window opened on 23rd October 2026 and remains open until 7th December 2026. It offers grants to clubs, community groups and organisations to improve access to water and protect the environment. The Paddle Trust raises money through donations and gives it away as grants.
grants.eligibility: Open to clubs, community groups and organisations across the UK.

grants.title: Neighbourhood Heritage: Grants for Communities
grants.summary: A new Historic England grant that supports communities to use heritage to shape the future of their local places. It funds projects that discover what people value about their neighbourhoods and help communities take part in local change.
grants.body: The grant supports communities to use heritage as a way of building confidence, strengthening local identity, creating new relationships and influencing decisions about where they live. Heritage is described broadly, covering more than historic buildings, sites and stories. Funding is aimed at projects that find out what people value about their neighbourhoods while improving how heritage can help communities take part in shaping local change.

sources.name: Green Allotments: New Allotment Site Fund

grants.title: The New Allotment Site Fund
grants.summary: Green Allotments buys land for new non-profit allotment sites in England, at up to £50,000 per acre, and grants a 30 year Peppercorn Lease to a self-managed allotment society. The fund does not give out money.
grants.body: The fund pays for the purchase of land for new allotment sites. Green Allotments keeps ownership of the land and grants the new allotment society a 30 year Peppercorn Lease with the intention to renew. The land is managed by the plotholders themselves through self-management of allotments, and Green Allotments will help the group constitute as an allotment society and pay the first year of National Allotment Society membership. Green Allotments is unlikely to fund land costing more than £50,000 per acre, and it prioritises as many new non-profit allotment sites as possible. Land must not be reserved for one group of people, as new allotments are rented first come first served to the public. Environmental stewardship, including no pesticides or herbicides, is part of the intention for the land. Applicants should find a piece of land first and share its location with a What3Words or Google Maps link.
grants.eligibility: Open to permanent residents in England aged 18 or over who want to create a new allotment site together. All tiers of councils and statutory organisations are excluded. Community Interest Companies are not eligible. Applicants cannot seek land for their own organisation, or land a community organisation already rents or owns. Groups must be willing to collaborate with Green Allotments and manage the land as an allotment society.
grants.how_to_apply: There is no form to complete. Contact Green Allotments by email or through its social media channels. Explain who you are and where you are based, give your contact details, and describe the land you have found, with a What3Words or Google Maps link. Say why the land would make a good allotment site and share any information about allotments in your area.

grants.title: Voices from the Frontline
grants.summary: Grants of £500 to £10,000 over 18 months for women's and girls' organisations to run campaigning and influencing work that helps women and girls use their voice to achieve change.
grants.body: The Voices from the Frontline fund supports campaigning and influencing work by women's and girls' organisations. Eligible activities include campaigning for changes in policy and laws, influencing central or local government and community leaders, training professionals who work with women and girls, gathering evidence or producing tools for campaigns, social media and media campaigns on specific issues, and training activists in campaigning, advocacy or public speaking. Grants range from £500 to £10,000 and are paid over 18 months. Applicants must meet Rosa's definition of a women's and girls' organisation, meaning it is run by, for and with women and girls. Groups that received a grant in round 8, awarded in March 2026, cannot apply. The application deadline was extended to 4pm on Tuesday 17 November 2026 because of a Microsoft outage affecting Rosa.
grants.eligibility: Organisations must meet Rosa's definition of a women's and girls' organisation: governed and led by women, a board where the chair is a woman and most members are women, a majority of women in the employee leadership team, a principal objective of working with women and/or girls, and a majority of beneficiaries who are women and/or girls. Must be not-for-profit, have a written governing document, a governing body of at least 3 unrelated members, a UK bank or building society account in the organisation's name with at least 2 unrelated signatories, at least one year of activity with annual accounts for a full year, and an appropriate safeguarding policy. Organisations that received a round 8 grant cannot apply.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the application guidance and FAQs and, if possible, attend a How to Apply webinar. Submit the brief online registration form, only if the organisation believes it is eligible. Then complete the application form using the link sent by email. Finally, send a video of no more than three minutes by WeTransfer explaining how the funding will be used. Both the application form and the video must be submitted by the deadline.

grants.title: Cash4Clubs
grants.summary: Unrestricted grants of £2,000 for grassroots community sports clubs and organisations across the UK and Ireland to support sport for social purpose. Applications are open until 1 January 2027.
grants.body: Cash4Clubs is a small grants scheme for community sports clubs and organisations. The funding is unrestricted, so groups decide what it is spent on, such as venue hire, utilities, equipment, coaching, volunteer expenses, kit, marketing, training, qualifications or insurances and affiliations. The grant is for activities that support a club to continue or grow its sports activities for adults. Each club can apply for one grant only. Awards cannot be split between different teams within a club, so clubs should decide where the funds are most needed. Amounts are £2,000 (or €2,000 in Ireland).
grants.eligibility: Grassroots community sports clubs and organisations across the UK and Ireland that use sport for social purpose. Support is for activities for adults. Only one grant can be made per club.
grants.how_to_apply: Start an online application from the Cash4Clubs website between 1 October 2026 and 1 January 2027. Winners are contacted after the deadline has passed.

grants.title: Garfield Weston Foundation grants
grants.summary: A family-founded grant-maker that gives money to charities across the UK in sectors including welfare, youth, community, environment, education, health, arts, heritage and faith. The Foundation donates over £150 million each year.
grants.body: The Foundation supports a wide range of charities doing work that makes a positive difference across the UK. Its areas of interest include welfare, youth, community, environment, education, health, arts, heritage and faith. The Foundation's website describes grants for operating and core costs, and for specific activity, project or capital projects. Groups should read the application guidelines and eligibility quiz on the Foundation's website before applying.
grants.eligibility: Charities working in the UK. Applicants should check the eligibility quiz and application guidelines on the Foundation's website.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the application guidelines and complete the eligibility quiz on the Foundation's website, then submit an application through the online application system.

sources.name: Better Community Business Network: Grant Initiative

grants.title: BCBN Grant Initiative
grants.summary: One-off grants of up to £3,000 for registered charities and small credible community projects in the UK that benefit local communities. Term 3 applications are described as opening soon, and the 2026 initiative concludes in November 2026.
grants.body: The Grant Initiative provides small one-off grant awards to charities and local community projects that can show a positive impact on the communities they serve. Each project may receive up to £3,000, and BCBN distributes up to £36,000 a year across the UK. Grants cover project costs and purchases such as equipment. They do not cover core or running costs, staff costs, salaries, venue hire, bills, travel and accommodation, retrospective costs, endowments, loans, deficits or general appeals. Applications to support fundraising, campaigning or any political party are not accepted. A successful organisation may receive only one grant in a year. Applications for grants above £3,000 may be turned down. Joint funders and partnerships must be listed where a project is part-funded. Grantees report on how the money was used with an evaluation form and photographs.
grants.eligibility: Open to non-profit organisations, charities and community groups, including local branches of national charities, that work for the betterment of local communities through charitable initiatives. Projects must be UK based, excluding Northern Ireland, address a community issue and provide benefits to the local community. Organisations must be registered with a recognised body such as the Charity Commission or Companies House for at least 18 months, have annual accounts available and submitted, and provide an articles of association or constitution if selected. Organisations must be operational for at least one year and have independently reviewed or audited accounts. Overseas activities, individual sponsorship and companies limited by shares or other commercial companies are excluded.
grants.how_to_apply: Take the eligibility quiz on the funder's page before submitting an application. The online application opens when the Term 3 period begins. Applications are reviewed within the relevant grant term, and successful applicants are contacted by email.

grants.title: Seedlings Foundation Grant Funds
grants.summary: Grants for activities for children and young people in West Yorkshire. There are two funding streams: one for providers working with children aged 0 to 5, and one for providers working with children and young people aged 6 to 19.
grants.body: The Foundation was formed to keep funds in Leeds for the benefit of children and young people. Its grants have gone to preschools, nurseries, outside play projects and special needs providers. There are two funding streams. One supports providers of childcare and activities for children aged 0 to 5. The other supports providers of care and activities for children and young people aged 6 to 19. Applications are assessed by the trustees on a rolling basis, so decisions can be made fairly quickly.
grants.eligibility: Organisations working with children and young people who operate within West Yorkshire. Applicants must meet the listed criteria on the funder's application criteria page.
grants.how_to_apply: Complete an application form and attach supporting documents such as a copy of your constitution, most recent accounts and safeguarding policy. Send by post or by email to the administrators, Community Matters (Yorkshire).

grants.title: Core Cost Funding
grants.summary: Unrestricted core funding of up to £7,500 for grassroots charitable organisations with people over 65 at the heart of their work.
grants.body: The Foundation awards unrestricted core funding to grassroots charitable organisations that have people over 65 at the heart of their work. Organisations that can show a strong alignment with the Foundation's charitable aims are invited to apply for unrestricted funding of up to £7,500. The Foundation says it will work with small organisations to keep the process simple, transparent and fair, and will help report on the impact of the grant. Organisations unsure whether core cost funding suits them can get in touch for advice first. The Foundation's organisations supporting people over 65 are expected to have an annual income under £250,000.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities and community groups with people over 65 at the heart of their work. Unrestricted funding is not available to Community Interest Companies. Organisations should have an annual income under £250,000.
grants.how_to_apply: Organisations that can demonstrate strong alignment with the Foundation's charitable aims are invited to apply. Contact the Foundation for advice if unsure whether core cost funding is right for you.

grants.title: Project Funding
grants.summary: Funding for new or existing programmes supporting people over 65 within an organisation.
grants.body: The Foundation invites applications for Project Funding to support a new or existing programme dedicated to supporting people over 65 within an organisation. This funding is typically restricted to the project. Applicants are encouraged to apply on a cost-recovery basis. The Foundation asks interested organisations to get in touch for more information. Organisations supporting people over 65 are expected to have an annual income under £250,000.
grants.eligibility: Open to registered charities, community groups and community interest companies limited by guarantee. The programme must support people over 65.
grants.how_to_apply: Get in touch with the Foundation for more information before applying.

grants.title: Movement for Good £1,000 Draws
grants.summary: Nominate a charity, CIC or non-profit for a chance to win one of 100 £1,000 awards in each of the regular draws. Nominations are open all year.
grants.body: Benefact Group gives away its available profits to good causes through the Movement for Good programme. Supporters nominate the charities, community interest companies or non-profits they choose, and nominated organisations are entered into prize draws. Each regular draw offers 100 awards of £1,000. Nominations can be made at any time through the year, and the draws take place in set windows within that period. The draws are open to registered charities, non-registered charities, churches and Community Interest Companies. Organisations do not apply directly; a supporter must nominate them.
grants.eligibility: Open to registered charities, non-registered charities, churches and Community Interest Companies. Organisations are nominated by supporters rather than applying directly.
grants.how_to_apply: Supporters nominate a charity, CIC or non-profit online at the draws page. The nomination takes about one minute.

grants.title: Movement for Good 12 Days of Giving
grants.summary: A December round of the Movement for Good draws offering 240 awards of £1,000 to nominated charities, CICs and non-profits. Nominations run from 1 to 16 December.
grants.body: The 12 Days of Giving is a December round of the Movement for Good £1,000 draws run by Benefact Group. Supporters nominate charities, community interest companies or non-profits, and nominated organisations are entered into the draw. The round offers 240 awards of £1,000 each, the largest single batch of the year. Nominations are open from 1 to 16 December. The round is open to registered charities, non-registered charities, churches and Community Interest Companies. Organisations are nominated by supporters rather than applying directly.
grants.eligibility: Open to registered charities, non-registered charities, churches and Community Interest Companies. Organisations are nominated by supporters rather than applying directly.
grants.how_to_apply: Supporters nominate a charity, CIC or non-profit online during the 1 to 16 December window. The nomination takes about one minute.

grants.title: Small Change Big Difference Fund
grants.summary: Donations of £250 to £2,500 to UK registered charities providing urgent support or relief to people experiencing financial hardship. Charities must be nominated by a Yorkshire Building Society member or colleague.
grants.body: The Small Change Big Difference Fund is run by the Yorkshire Building Society Charitable Foundation and is funded by pence of interest from members' accounts through the Society's SCBD scheme. Trustees aim to support charities that provide urgent support or relief to people facing financial hardship, such as food banks, to help them meet immediate needs. Donations range from £250 to £2,500. The Foundation particularly welcomes nominations from charities working in areas of deprivation and from charities with an income of less than £100,000. A charity cannot apply directly: it must be nominated by a Yorkshire Building Society member or colleague. Nominations are accepted on an ongoing basis, with quarterly review by the trustees. Decisions for nominations made from 1 January to 31 March are given in May, from 1 April to 30 June in August, from 1 July to 30 September in November, and from 1 October to 31 December in February. Successful charities receive payment at the end of each quarter through a payment partner.
grants.eligibility: Must be a UK registered charity (Charity Commission for England and Wales, Charity Commission for Northern Ireland or Scottish Charity Regulator) with annual returns submitted on time. The work must provide urgent support or relief to people experiencing financial hardship and must benefit people in the UK. The charity must have been nominated by a Yorkshire Building Society member or colleague and must not have received a Charitable Foundation donation in the last 2 years. Not considered: community interest companies, unregistered community or voluntary organisations, animal welfare charities, charities serving a specific sector of the community selected on political or religious grounds, and charities with beneficiaries outside the UK.
grants.how_to_apply: A Yorkshire Building Society member or colleague submits a nomination through the online nomination form. Members or colleagues unable to use the online form can visit their nearest branch. Nominations pass basic eligibility checks, then trustees make decisions each quarter.

grants.title: Foodbank Fundamentals Fund
grants.summary: Grants of up to £1,000 for food banks and food providers to buy essential food, hygiene items, white goods, storage and fuel for food deliveries. The application window is currently closed.
grants.body: The fund supports organisations whose core purpose is distributing food and alleviating food poverty in their local community. Eligible costs include essential food, basic hygiene items, white goods such as fridges and freezers, storage and fixtures such as shelving, and fuel for delivering food to isolated people. Groups must have a total annual income of £250,000 or below and a constitution, a safeguarding policy with two named safeguarding leads, and a bank account in the group's name that accepts cheques. Branches or projects of larger organisations must show separate accounts, accounts and constitution. Grants are paid by cheque. Only one branch or sub-group per community can receive support. Funding must be used within 6 months of receipt.
grants.eligibility: Not-for-profit groups whose primary aim is food distribution and provision, such as food banks, community pantries, social supermarkets, soup kitchens and breakfast clubs. Based in and benefiting people in the UK. Not open to public bodies (except PTAs), groups affiliated with a political party, animal charities, groups involving alcohol, or groups already funded by Asda Foundation in 2026. Religious organisations serving only people of one faith are excluded.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the grant guidance and check eligibility through the Eligibility Check on the Asda Foundation website. Then register or log in to the SmartSimple grant portal and complete the application under Funding Opportunities. Decisions are emailed within 12 weeks.

grants.title: Home Improvement Grants
grants.summary: Grants of up to £10,000 for registered charities to create or improve homes and the places where people live, such as decorating, roof repairs, garden refurbishment and new rooms or buildings.
grants.body: The B&Q Foundation awards grants to charities that are creating or improving homes so that more people in our communities have a place to feel at home. The fund covers projects such as decorating, fixing roofs, refurbishing garden space, upgrading key fixtures and fittings, and creating new buildings or rooms. Funding of up to £10,000 is available, and the foundation says it works with many different types of charity as long as the project is about improving homes and where people live. Applications are made through Neighbourly. Due to high application volumes, it may take up to 12 weeks after the deadline to hear the outcome.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities only. The project must be about improving or creating homes or the places where people live.
grants.how_to_apply: Check the grant criteria in the guidance and FAQs, then apply online through Neighbourly if your charity meets them. The foundation will review applications and contact you, which may take up to 12 weeks after the deadline.

grants.title: Home-Starter Kit Grants
grants.summary: Grants of up to £10,000 for registered charities to improve homes and the places where people live, applied for through Neighbourly.
grants.body: The Home-Starter Kit grant is one of two grant funds run by the B&Q Foundation for charities that are creating or improving homes so that more people in our communities have a place to feel at home. The foundation supports projects such as decorating, fixing roofs, refurbishing garden space, upgrading key fixtures and fittings, and creating new buildings or rooms. Funding of up to £10,000 is available across both grant funds. Applications are made through Neighbourly, and decisions may take up to 12 weeks after the deadline.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities only. The project must be about improving or creating homes or the places where people live.
grants.how_to_apply: Check the grant criteria in the guidance and FAQs, then apply online through Neighbourly if your charity meets them. The foundation will review applications and contact you, which may take up to 12 weeks after the deadline.

grants.title: Charitable Grants
grants.summary: The Weavers' Company Benevolent Fund makes grants to projects supporting people in trouble, especially ex-offenders and young people in the criminal justice system. Preference goes to innovative new projects. Grant amounts are not stated.
grants.body: The Weavers' Company Benevolent Fund was set up in 1973 and aims mainly to support people in trouble, particularly ex-offenders and young people involved in the Criminal Justice System. Preference is given to pump-priming new projects that are innovative and could serve as a model elsewhere. The current priority is helping offenders and ex-offenders build skills and capability to move into sustainable work. The Company also supports charities working with less popular groups within the criminal justice sector, and projects working specifically with young people aged 16 to 25 who are involved with the Criminal Justice System. Shortlisted projects are visited by a member of the Company. The Charitable Grants Committee meets three times a year to decide grants and amounts. The total awarded each year depends on the Company's investment income.
grants.eligibility: Projects must fit the Fund's criteria, mainly work with ex-offenders, people in the criminal justice system and young people involved with that system aged 16 to 25. General youth development projects are not the focus.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the charitable grants guidelines and the applying for a charitable grant page. Shortlisted projects are visited by a member of the Company before the Charitable Grants Committee decides on grants.

grants.title: Hillards Charitable Trust grants
grants.funder: Gay and Peter Hartley's Hillards Charitable Trust
grants.summary: Grants for independent, non-profit, voluntary and community groups providing social support in communities once served by Hillards stores. Grants are normally one-off up to £1,000, with two £10,000 grants available where they can have significant impact.
grants.body: The Trust supports care for older people such as luncheon clubs, outings, winter aid, activities that combat isolation and social activities. It also funds volunteer schemes, respite care and hospices, support for less able people with physical or mental health needs, children's charities that enhance sports or social opportunities, church based projects with a proven outreach factor, and education support such as reading support, literacy and one to one help. Grants are normally one-off and up to £1,000. The Trust makes two grants of £10,000 each where such a grant can deliver a significant impact for an organisation. Maintenance and driver training support for minibuses is considered. The Trust does not fund capital projects unless majority funding has been pledged, animal welfare or wildlife bodies, medical research, loans, sponsorship or fundraising events, or activities run by local authority employees. Organisations that received a Trust grant in the preceding 18 months are excluded.
grants.eligibility: Independent, locally managed, non-profit, voluntary and community-based organisations that provide social support to the communities once served by Hillards stores. Organisations with more than 33% of their income from statutory funding are not eligible. Grant-giving organisations, national charities without autonomy in the Trust's area, and bodies that received a Trust grant in the preceding 18 months are excluded. Individuals' personal needs, promotion of religion and university or college fees are not funded.
grants.how_to_apply: Use the Trust's online application form on the application page.

sources.name: True Colours Trust: UK small grants

grants.title: UK Small Grants
grants.summary: Grants of up to £10,000, open all year, for local organisations supporting disabled children, children with life-limiting conditions and their families. Many grants are smaller than the maximum.
grants.body: The UK Small Grants programme supports projects for disabled children, children with life-limiting conditions and their families, including activities for siblings, bereavement support, parent-led peer support, whole-family respite, and specialised play or leisure access. It also funds renovation or upgrading of hydrotherapy pools and multi-sensory rooms, minibuses and specialised play equipment. Organisations working with children and young people aged 0 to 25 can apply. The Trust is particularly keen to hear from organisations working in areas of high deprivation, and funded groups must be open to children and families of all faiths, backgrounds and cultures. The Trust cannot fund the same organisation in consecutive years. After a grant, a group must wait at least two years from receiving the payment before reapplying, and after an unsuccessful application it must wait at least one year.
grants.eligibility: Open to UK registered charitable organisations and community interest companies delivering projects in the UK, with annual income below £350,000. Organisations must have a full year of accounts, so newly registered groups cannot apply. Condition-specific organisations, schools, Parent Teacher Associations and 'Friends of' groups supporting specific schools, and local authorities are not eligible. Funding is not available for overnight activities, holidays or short breaks, wish-granting, regranting, projects outside the UK, or organisations set up to support one individual only. Groups with a live grant or a payment within the last two years cannot apply.
grants.how_to_apply: Complete the eligibility quiz first, then launch the online application form. Have your charity or CIC number, accounts, safeguarding policy, budget and service user details ready, as the form cannot be saved part way through. Applications are accepted at any time, with a decision aimed for within twelve weeks.

grants.title: Communities Fund
grants.summary: Match funding for crowdfunding projects by UK small charities, social enterprises and local causes working on climate action or financial wellbeing. Every individual donation up to £250 is matched, with up to £25,000 per organisation in a calendar year.
grants.body: The Communities Fund matches individual donations raised through a crowdfunding page on the Communities Fund platform. Each eligible donation is matched up to £250, so a £5 donation becomes £10 and a £250 donation becomes £500. Projects must relate to one of two themes: climate action or financial wellbeing. The fund is open to a wide range of causes, including work with children and young people, older people, health and mental health, disability, arts and culture, the environment and community development. Projects can also draw on volunteering support alongside the match funding. An organisation can receive up to £25,000 in a calendar year, which may be split across up to two projects. Match funding is available for six weeks from when a crowdfunding project launches, or from approval if the project is already live. Organisations can reapply after a previous project.
grants.eligibility: UK small charities, social enterprises and local causes whose project supports climate action or financial wellbeing. Projects must be able to explain clearly how they tie into one of these two themes. Organisations must meet the full eligibility criteria published on the Communities Fund site.
grants.how_to_apply: Check the eligibility criteria first. Create a project page on the Communities Fund crowdfunding platform, explain how the project links to climate action or financial wellbeing, and spread the word to supporters. Match funding applies to eligible donations received within six weeks of the project launching.

grants.title: Arnold Clark Community Fund: Cost of Living
grants.summary: Funding for local charities and projects that help people facing hardship due to the rising cost of living.
grants.body: The Cost of Living strand supports local charities and projects that help people facing hardship because of rising living costs. The Arnold Clark Community Fund as a whole supports registered UK charities and community groups located within 50 miles of an Arnold Clark branch. Funding should provide immediate relief, as the fund cannot commit to funding at a later date.
grants.eligibility: Registered UK charities and community groups located within 50 miles of an Arnold Clark branch. Organisations must be UK-based and provide direct support to people and communities in the UK.

grants.title: Gear Up For Sport
grants.summary: Free kits and training equipment for youth sports teams across the UK, given away by the Arnold Clark Community Fund.
grants.body: Gear Up For Sport gives away hundreds of free kits and training equipment to youth sports teams across the UK. The programme sits within the Arnold Clark Community Fund, which welcomes applications from registered charities and community groups located within 50 miles of an Arnold Clark branch.
grants.eligibility: Youth sports teams across the UK. The Arnold Clark Community Fund as a whole is limited to organisations within 50 miles of an Arnold Clark branch.

grants.title: Arnold Clark Community Fund: Our Communities Support
grants.summary: Funding for local charities and organisations that provide important services, strengthen communities and help them build a better future.
grants.body: Our Communities Support funds local charities and organisations that provide important services and strengthen communities. The Arnold Clark Community Fund welcomes applications from registered charities and community groups located within 50 miles of an Arnold Clark branch. Funding should provide immediate relief, as the fund cannot commit to funding at a later date.
grants.eligibility: Registered UK charities and community groups located within 50 miles of an Arnold Clark branch. Organisations must be UK-based and provide direct support to people and communities in the UK.

grants.title: Tesco Fruit & Veg Grants
grants.summary: Grants of up to £1,500 for schools, registered charities and not-for-profit groups supporting children to get better access to fruit and vegetables. Final amounts are set by a customer vote in Tesco stores.
grants.body: The fund aims to improve children's access to free fruit and vegetables and support a healthy, nutritious diet. Eligible projects include providing fruit or healthy snacks in school, breakfast or holiday clubs, smoothie or cooking classes, and growing or gardening projects that teach how fruit and vegetables grow. Half time power for a sports club has also been mentioned as an example. Every four months, three local projects are selected to go to a customer vote in Tesco stores across the UK. Every shortlisted project receives funding, and the amount depends on how many blue token votes it receives, from £500 up to £1,500. Groundwork, Tesco's community charity partner, manages the application process. Groundwork is working with greenspace scotland to support successful projects in Scotland.
grants.eligibility: Open to schools, registered charities and not-for-profit organisations that support children and young people. Projects must improve access to fruit and vegetables and support the nutrition of children and young people across the UK. Applicants need the postcode of their project to find their local Tesco store.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the guidance notes on the funder's page. Find your local Tesco store using the store locator and your project postcode. Submit your application using the online form. Tesco customers and colleagues can also nominate a school or children's group for consideration.

grants.title: npower Business Solutions Foundation
grants.summary: Grants of up to £100,000 for projects that decarbonise, support responsible businesses, promote social innovation or champion local skills and employment in communities near the Solihull and Leeds offices.
grants.body: The foundation supports projects that help create stronger, greener and more sustainable local communities. It seeks work that decarbonises and safeguards the environment, supports the growth of responsible businesses, promotes social innovation, or champions local skills or employment. Funding is offered in bands depending on organisation turnover. Organisations with turnover of £50,000 or less can apply for up to £19,999. Organisations with turnover above £50,000 can apply for up to £19,999, £20,000 to £39,999, or £40,000 to £100,000. The project must be completed within 12 months of funding being received. Applications are open with no deadline. The panel aims to make award decisions quarterly. A short video of up to two minutes is required with every application. Charis Grants Limited manages the fund and administers the awards.
grants.eligibility: Not-for-profit organisations and educational institutions that have been registered for more than two years and are based within a 50 mile radius of the Solihull (B91 3ES) or Leeds (LS15 8ZB) offices, or national organisations with operations in those areas. Eligible legal forms include companies limited by guarantee, registered charities, CIOs and SCIOs, CICs, religious organisations (only where the project benefits the wider community and has no religious content), co-operative and community benefit societies, schools, colleges, universities, academy trusts and other education establishments, and CASCs registered with HMRC. Parish councils are not eligible. Organisations must be able to provide accounts confirming turnover or income.
grants.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Charis Grants application portal. The form can be completed in stages using the emailed link. Once submitted, upload supporting documents. Required items include a short video, a safeguarding policy and financial accounts. For requests over £20,000, a project plan and risk register are also needed. Decisions are made by quarterly panel review, with awards issued in the months after each quarter closes.

sources.name: Masonic Charitable Foundation: grants to charities

grants.title: Warburtons Foundation financial giving
grants.summary: Financial giving from the Warburtons Foundation supports projects, activities and organisations with charitable aims that directly benefit families.
grants.body: The Warburtons Foundation runs a financial giving programme to support projects, activities and organisations that have charitable aims and will bring direct benefit to families. The foundation's stated ambition is to donate £100k a year to local charities through its community grant programme. The foundation also supports communities through product donations and education programmes, and its community and charity champions make decisions on local financial giving.

grants.title: Warburtons Foundation product donations
grants.summary: Warburtons donates bread and other products to food banks, breakfast clubs and other community groups that support families facing food insecurity.
grants.body: The Warburtons Foundation offers product donations to support local community activities and food redistribution. Its stated target is to donate 2 million products each year to food banks, breakfast clubs and other groups. Donations focus on affordable access to healthy staples such as bread.

grants.title: Screwfix Foundation grants
grants.summary: Grants of around £5,000 for registered charities and not for profit organisations helping people in need. Funding supports repair, maintenance, improvement or construction of homes, community buildings and other buildings.
grants.body: The Screwfix Foundation offers grants of around £5,000 to local registered charities and not for profit organisations. Funding is aimed at projects that repair, maintain, improve or build homes, community buildings and other buildings. Applications are reviewed individually by the Foundation team each quarter, with review dates in March, June, September and December. Organisations must help people in need, whether through financial hardship, sickness, distress or other disadvantage in the UK. The Foundation also has a partnership with Hospice UK to provide improvement grants to hospices, and a youth trade skills initiative with Volunteer It Yourself.
grants.eligibility: Must be a registered charity or not for profit organisation. Must help people in need through financial hardship, sickness, distress or other disadvantages in the UK. Must be seeking funding for projects relating to the repair, maintenance, improvement or construction of homes, community buildings and other buildings. The full eligibility criteria are set out in a separate document linked from the funder's page.
grants.how_to_apply: Check the full eligibility criteria, then complete the online funding application form. Applications are reviewed quarterly, with review dates in March, June, September and December.

grants.title: Charles and Elsie Sykes Trust grants
grants.summary: The Trust awards grants to registered charities, exempt or excepted charities and CICs working mainly for beneficiaries in the Yorkshire area, with priority for poverty, disability, homelessness, domestic abuse, addiction, children, young people and older people.
grants.body: The Trust is a charitable foundation established in 1954 that gives grants to help qualifying organisations achieve their charitable goals, primarily for beneficiaries in the Yorkshire area. The Trust is particularly interested in work that helps people suffering from poverty, disability, homelessness, domestic abuse and addiction, and work with children, young people and the elderly. It also mentions music and singing linked to education, equipment for local hospitals, and public health initiatives. For medical research it prefers Yorkshire-based research institutions. Applications are considered regardless of the size or location of the charity, although certain qualifying criteria apply.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities, exempt or excepted charities, and community interest companies (CICs). Work should primarily benefit people in the Yorkshire area.

grants.title: Enterprise Gateway Fund
grants.summary: A £6 million, three-year fund that will pick at least four Intermediary Partners to give onward grants and enterprise development support to small VCSE organisations and social entrepreneurs. Intermediaries can apply for £500,000 to £1.5 million.
grants.body: The Enterprise Gateway Fund helps small voluntary, community and social enterprise organisations and social entrepreneurs explore trading ideas, test whether they could work, and build the skills needed to develop new sources of earned income. It is aimed at early-stage organisations and places where enterprise support is currently limited, including areas in the most deprived IMD 1 to 3 category. The Foundation will not fund small organisations or individuals directly. It is inviting organisations to become Intermediary Partners, which will recruit participants, make onward grants and deliver a package of enterprise development support, peer learning and networking. Intermediaries must show an annual income of at least £500,000 and must have audited or independently examined accounts for at least a year. Intermediaries do not need to work across the whole UK. The fund is UK wide, with £4 million ring fenced for asset-locked organisations in England and £2 million for non-constituted organisations and individuals. Applicants must work within one or more of the Foundation's priority areas: Getting Started, Building Independence and Safer Futures.
grants.eligibility: Intended for organisations applying to become Intermediary Partners. Intermediaries need an annual income of at least £500,000, a track record of supporting enterprise or trading activity, experience of managing onward grants, and established networks reaching underserved communities. Intermediaries must have a year of audited or independently examined accounts. Small organisations and social entrepreneurs cannot apply directly to the Foundation. Participants recruited by intermediaries must be constituted VCSEs in England with turnover under £500,000, or other asset-locked or non-constituted organisations and individuals working across the UK, and must work in one of the Foundation's priority areas.
grants.how_to_apply: Check eligibility using the online eligibility checker. Eligible organisations submit an expression of interest by 5pm on 25 November 2026, after it opens on 28 October 2026. Invited organisations submit a full application by 5pm on 22 January 2027, followed by a phone conversation in late January or February 2027. Intermediary Partners are expected to be told in the first week of April 2027. Application support calls are available before the expression of interest deadline.

grants.title: Enterprise Gateway
grants.summary: Funding, practical support and capacity building to help enterprise ideas come to life.
grants.body: The Enterprise Gateway is one of the Henry Smith Foundation's open grant programmes. It brings enterprise ideas to life through funding, practical support and capacity building. The programme sits under the Foundation's priority areas of supporting families, helping young people move into adulthood, and supporting people to rebuild their lives. Full criteria are on the programme page.

grants.title: Clergy
grants.summary: Christian grants supporting initiatives that promote the wellbeing of Anglican clergy.
grants.body: The Clergy programme is a Christian grants programme that supports initiatives promoting Anglican clergy wellbeing. It is listed as open on the Henry Smith Foundation grants page. Check the programme page for the full criteria and what each grant can cover.

sources.name: Henry Smith Charity: explore our grants

grants.title: Metcalfe Smith Trust grants for disability and long-term illness
grants.summary: Grants to help people and local organisations in Leeds affected by mental or physical disability or long-term illness with necessary costs such as equipment, household items and convalescent or respite care. Grants are usually £250 to £2,500.
grants.body: The Trust makes grants for the relief of hardship connected with sickness, ill-health or disability. Support can cover essential equipment, household items, convalescent or respite care, and other necessary costs linked to disability or long-term illness. The Trust funds applicants in the Leeds area. National organisations are considered only where a project specifically benefits people in Leeds. Grants are usually £250 to £2,500, and emergency grants of up to £150 are available between Trustee meetings. The Trust does not fund general appeals, research, general fundraising, administrative costs, fees or salaries, tuition or course fees, rent, utility bills, general living costs, holidays or short breaks, or retrospective costs. Recurrent grants are not normally made, so ongoing funding should not be assumed.
grants.eligibility: Open to individuals and organisations in the Leeds area affected by mental or physical disability or long-term illness. National organisations can apply only where the project specifically benefits people in Leeds. The Trust does not fund general appeals, research, general fundraising, administrative costs, fees or salaries, tuition or course fees, rent, utility bills, general living costs, holidays or short breaks, or retrospective costs.
grants.how_to_apply: Applications for the Trustee meeting on 10 May 2027 need to be received by the end of April 2027. The following Trustee meeting is on 18 October 2027.

grants.title: Allen Lane Foundation grants
grants.summary: The Foundation runs seven funding programmes and accepts applications all year. Applicants first complete an eligibility questionnaire, and successful projects must fit the aims of one of the programmes.
grants.body: The Allen Lane Foundation funds work that fits the specific aims of one of its seven funding programmes. Current programme areas include asylum seekers and refugees, Gypsy and Traveller communities, offenders and ex-offenders, older people, people affected by violence or abuse, people with mental health problems, and young people. Groups should check the exclusions list before applying. Applications can be made at any time and are processed throughout the year. Trustees consider grant applications three times a year, generally in February, June and October. Applications received up to early December are expected to be considered at the February 2027 meeting. Processing an application and making a grant usually takes between two and six months. The Foundation aims to respond within a couple of weeks with initial thoughts, and may ask for further information or arrange a visit.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the funding criteria and exclusions, then complete the online eligibility questionnaire. If the answers confirm eligibility, you are directed to the application form. Contact the Foundation by email if you have difficulty accessing the quiz or forms.

grants.title: Community Impact Grants
grants.summary: Grants for projects that address social challenges and help congregations grow across the UK and Ireland.
grants.body: This programme supports projects that address social challenges and help churches and Christian charities grow their congregations and community reach across the UK and Ireland. Benefact Trust is one of the UK's largest Christian grant-giving charities. Applicants should check the programme's own application guidance for current details.
grants.eligibility: Christian churches and Christian charities working in the UK and Ireland.
grants.how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply for a Community Impact Grant link on the Benefact Trust grants page.

grants.title: Building Grants
grants.summary: Grants to protect and enhance Christian buildings in the UK and Ireland. The programme now includes Roof Alarms.
grants.body: This programme funds building repairs and improvements to Christian buildings across the UK and Ireland. It now includes Roof Alarms. Applicants should check the programme's own guidance for current details on eligible works and application steps.
grants.eligibility: Christian churches and Christian organisations responsible for Christian buildings in the UK and Ireland.
grants.how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply for a Building Grant link on the Benefact Trust grants page.

grants.title: Methodist Grants
grants.summary: Grants supporting Methodist building and repair projects across the UK and Ireland.
grants.body: This programme supports Methodist building and repair projects across the UK and Ireland. Methodist organisations can also apply to other relevant Benefact Trust grant programmes. Applicants should check the programme's own guidance for current details.
grants.eligibility: Methodist organisations in the UK and Ireland.
grants.how_to_apply: Use the How to Apply for a Methodist Grant link on the Benefact Trust grants page.

grants.title: Brelms Trust grants
grants.summary: The Brelms Trust offers grants to charities in Yorkshire that benefit Yorkshire communities. Grants range from £1,000 to £7,000 per year, one-off or for up to three consecutive years.
grants.body: The Trust gives priority to charities working at the heart of communities to tackle disadvantage and provide sustainable benefit to the community. Applications from a diversity of charitable organisations are welcomed. Grants can cover staff salaries, volunteer expenses, running costs and direct service provision. The Trust does not generally support the total cost of a project, so applicants should show that wider funding plans are in place. Grants are awarded from £1,000 to a maximum of £7,000 per year, either as a one-off amount or for up to three consecutive years, giving a maximum of £21,000 over three years. Trustees meet quarterly to make awards, and applications are assessed throughout the year.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities and charitable incorporated organisations based in Yorkshire that directly benefit Yorkshire communities. Priority goes to charities working at the heart of communities to tackle disadvantage.

grants.title: Connecting Communities
grants.summary: Grants of up to £20,000 for registered charities to breathe new life into local spaces, bring people together and keep vital local services open and accessible.
grants.body: The Connecting Communities scheme offers grant funding to registered charities. It is aimed at projects that help breathe new life into local spaces, bring people together and secure vital local services so they remain open and accessible for generations to come. Grants of up to £20,000 are available. The Foundation has said it has donated almost £50 million to registered charities since 2015, and its funding covers charities across England, Scotland and Wales.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities only. The scheme is open to charities in the communities the Foundation serves across England, Scotland and Wales.

grants.title: Match Funding
grants.summary: The Foundation matches money raised by Morrisons colleagues for registered charities they support, giving a cash boost to their fundraising.
grants.body: Match funding supports registered charities that Morrisons colleagues fundraise for. The Foundation provides a cash boost to these efforts, helping colleagues' fundraising from stores, depots, factories and head office go further. The fund depends on a Morrisons colleague fundraising for a registered charity, so charities need to be connected with a colleague who is raising money for them.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities that a Morrisons colleague fundraises for.

sources.name: Health Data Research UK: Take the Lead community grants

grants.title: Migration Fund
grants.summary: Funds work that supports a world where everyone is free to move and no one is forced to move. Grants of up to £60,000 per year for 3 to 4 years, or up to £50,000 per year for 5 years.
grants.body: The Migration Fund supports charitable organisations working on migration and the freedom to move. Projects can run for three to five years. The foundation seeks to fund work outside London and across the UK. Only charitable work, as defined by the Charity Commission, is eligible. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Generally, decisions take around four months from application, and costs already incurred cannot be covered.
grants.eligibility: Charitable organisations only. The foundation only funds work that is charitable as defined by the Charity Commission. It actively seeks work outside London and across the UK. Costs already incurred cannot be covered.
grants.how_to_apply: Apply through the foundation's online application system. Sample application forms are available to view before applying. Generally, decisions take around four months from application.

grants.title: Youth Fund
grants.summary: Funds organisations working with young people aged 14 to 25 to drive change so future generations can thrive. Grants of up to £150,000 over 3 years.
grants.body: The Youth Fund supports organisations that work with young people aged 14 to 25 to bring about change. Grants can be up to £150,000 over three years. The foundation seeks to fund work outside London and across the UK. Only charitable work, as defined by the Charity Commission, is eligible. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Generally, decisions take around four months from application, and costs already incurred cannot be covered.
grants.eligibility: Charitable organisations working with young people aged 14 to 25. The foundation only funds work that is charitable as defined by the Charity Commission. It actively seeks work outside London and across the UK. Costs already incurred cannot be covered.
grants.how_to_apply: Apply through the foundation's online application system. Sample application forms are available to view before applying. Generally, decisions take around four months from application.

grants.title: Arts-based Learning Fund
grants.summary: Supports arts and cultural organisations working in partnership with schools to make arts-based learning a core part of education. Grants from £30,000 to £300,000, up to £100,000 per year.
grants.body: The Arts-based Learning Fund supports arts and cultural organisations to work in partnership with schools, so that arts-based learning becomes a core part of education. Projects can run for one to four years. The foundation seeks to fund work outside London and across the UK. Only charitable work, as defined by the Charity Commission, is eligible. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Generally, decisions take around four months from application, and costs already incurred cannot be covered.
grants.eligibility: Arts and cultural charitable organisations working in partnership with schools. The foundation only funds work that is charitable as defined by the Charity Commission. It actively seeks work outside London and across the UK. Costs already incurred cannot be covered.
grants.how_to_apply: Apply through the foundation's online application system. A stage one sample application form is available to view before applying. Generally, decisions take around four months from application.

sources.name: Parkinson's UK: grants for physical activity providers

grants.title: Sir George Martin Trust grants
grants.summary: Flexible one-off grants of £1,000 to £5,000 for running, capital and project costs. Open to West Yorkshire registered charities and CIOs that support economically and socially disadvantaged people.
grants.body: The Sir George Martin Trust aims to improve the well-being of economically and socially disadvantaged people in West Yorkshire. It gives flexible, one-off grants for running, capital and project costs, with grants of £3,000 to £4,000 currently the most common. Applicants must deliver support or activities that benefit economically and socially disadvantaged people living in West Yorkshire, and must have a head office or Charity Commission main administration address in West Yorkshire. Organisations need an income below £1 million and must be committed to a safe culture for staff, volunteers and beneficiaries. The Trust uses a two-stage process: a brief Expression of Interest followed by a full application, which is only available after contact with the Trust Manager. The trustees next meet to discuss applications in February 2027, and the online portal reopened for that meeting on 1 October 2026.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities and CIOs with a Charity Commission number, based in West Yorkshire, with head office or main administration address in West Yorkshire. Income must be below £1 million. Must deliver work benefiting economically and socially disadvantaged people in West Yorkshire. Community groups not registered with the Charity Commission, CICs, community benefit societies, co-operatives, schools, nurseries and playgroups are not eligible. Churches are only considered if they are registered charities.
grants.how_to_apply: Set up an account on the online portal and complete the brief Expression of Interest form. Contacting the Trust Manager first is optional. Full application is invited after the Trust Manager assesses the expression of interest.

grants.title: Help the Homeless capital project grants
grants.summary: A small trust offering grants of up to £5,000 towards capital projects for charities working wholly or mostly with homeless people. Running costs, salaries and IT equipment are not covered.
grants.body: The trust makes small grants towards capital projects only, such as buildings and capital works, for charities whose work is wholly or mostly focused on homelessness. It does not fund general community work, foodbanks or projects not focused on homelessness. Applications for core or running costs and salaries are not accepted, and requests for computers and IT equipment cannot be considered. The trust does not consider multi-year requests, and funding is limited, so applicants should check carefully that they meet the criteria before applying. A minimum of two years must pass between receiving a decision or grant from the trust and making a further application.
grants.eligibility: Open to registered charities registered with the Charity Commission in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or registered Scottish charities. The charity must have an annual turnover of less than £500,000. The charity must work wholly or mostly with homeless people. Applications must be for capital projects; running costs, core costs and salaries are not eligible, and requests for computers and IT equipment are not considered.
grants.how_to_apply: Complete the trust's online application form by 5pm on the quarterly deadline. Deadlines fall on 20 March, 20 June, 20 September and 20 December each year. Applications by post or email are no longer accepted. The trustees' decision is sent within eight weeks of each deadline.

grants.title: Small Grants Programme
grants.summary: Grants of up to £500 for smaller requests that provide recreational opportunities or relate to public open space in the pre-1974 City of Leeds boundary. Open all year and administered by Voluntary Action Leeds.
grants.body: The Small Grants Programme supports smaller funding requests of up to £500 for projects that offer recreational opportunities to people, or that relate to the use of public open space. Projects must serve people living within the pre-1974 boundary of the City of Leeds, roughly Leeds postcodes LS1 to LS17, excluding areas previously in Wetherby Rural District Council, such as Thorner. The programme is open all year round and is administered by Voluntary Action Leeds. It considers applications from constituted community groups as well as registered charities. Grants are given on a single-year basis and longer term funding is not the norm. Applicants may submit one application per calendar year, with each assessed on its own merit.
grants.eligibility: Applicants must be registered charities, exempt or excepted charities, industrial and provident societies, or constituted community groups. The work must be wholly charitable and must provide recreational opportunities or relate to public open space. Projects must serve people residing in the pre-1974 boundary of the City of Leeds, roughly Leeds postcodes LS1 to LS17, but not areas previously within Wetherby Rural District Council such as Thorner.
grants.how_to_apply: Applications are made through the Small Grants Programme page, which is administered by Voluntary Action Leeds. The programme is open all year round.

grants.title: Main Grants Programme
grants.summary: Grants for requests above £500 that provide facilities for recreation or preserve public open space in Leeds, and support children, young people, older people, the wider community and the arts.
grants.body: The Main Grants Programme covers funding requests above £500 that fall outside the Small Grants Programme. Grants are awarded for the provision of facilities for recreation and for the preservation of public open space. The trust also receives applications to support children and young people, older people, the wider community and the arts. Projects must serve people residing in the pre-1974 boundary of the City of Leeds, roughly Leeds postcodes LS1 to LS17, excluding areas previously within Wetherby Rural District Council. The programme is open to registered charities and constituted voluntary or community groups. Grants are given on a single-year basis and longer term funding is not the norm. Applicants may submit one application per calendar year, with each assessed on its own merit.
grants.eligibility: Open to registered charities and constituted voluntary or community groups. Requests must be above £500 and fall outside the Small Grants Programme. Projects must provide recreation facilities or preserve public open space, or support children and young people, older people, the wider community or the arts. Projects must serve people residing in the pre-1974 boundary of the City of Leeds, roughly Leeds postcodes LS1 to LS17, excluding areas previously within Wetherby Rural District Council such as Thorner.
grants.how_to_apply: Applications are made through the Main Grants Programme page. Applicants may submit one application per calendar year.

grants.title: Jordan Sinnott Foundation Trust grants
grants.summary: The trust makes grants to community groups and individuals to help vulnerable and underprivileged children and young adults access sport and healthy recreation.
grants.body: The Jordan Sinnott Foundation Trust was set up in honour of Jordan Sinnott, a professional footballer, and aims to make sport accessible to people less privileged. Its mission is to support vulnerable and underprivileged children and young adults to access healthy recreation and sporting activities. The trust relies on donations to fund its grants, which support children and young adults with access to recreation and sport. The homepage mentions past support for a range of groups, including a power chair football club and a hockey club.
grants.eligibility: Grants are available to community groups and individuals. The grants are aimed at vulnerable and underprivileged children and young adults who need access to sport and recreation.

grants.title: Core and Project funding
grants.summary: Core and project grants for not-for-profit organisations working with children and young people aged 18 or under across the UK. Grants range from £1,000 to £40,000 per year for up to three years, with no application deadline.
grants.body: BBC Children in Need invests in positive relationships that strengthen children's wellbeing and help them handle the challenges in their lives. It offers Core and Project funding, which can cover running costs or specific project work. Applications can be made at any time. Available grants range from £1,000 to £40,000 per year and can be awarded for up to three years. Organisations must first attend a pre-application advice session, where the majority of their work is delivered, before submitting an Expression of Interest. The funder does not fund work that statutory bodies such as schools, local authorities or the NHS have a duty to provide. Organisations must meet its minimum standards for grantmaking, including taking full responsibility for finance, governance and safeguarding.
grants.eligibility: Must be a not-for-profit organisation working with children and young people aged 18 or under. Must meet the funder's minimum standards for grantmaking and take full responsibility for finance, governance and safeguarding during delivery. Statutory bodies such as schools, local authorities and the NHS are not eligible for work they have a duty to provide. Previous grant holders must also attend a pre-application session before applying again.
grants.how_to_apply: Read what the funder supports and check eligibility against its minimum standards. Attend a pre-application advice session, then submit an Expression of Interest through the online form.

grants.title: Running costs grants
grants.summary: Grants towards the running costs of small registered charities in England and Wales, helping them sustain their existing work. Usually up to £3,000 a year, for up to three years.
grants.body: The Trust makes grants that contribute towards the running costs of small registered charities. It only funds running costs, not new capital projects.
