Grants are normally up to £3,000 per year, and the Trust will fund for up to three years. Most grants are for more than one year because the Trust likes to support ongoing needs. The Trust only funds work that focuses specifically on its priority groups. Charities must have a total annual expenditure of less than £50,000. Community interest companies are not funded.
grants.eligibility: Registered charities in England and Wales with total annual expenditure of less than £50,000. Community interest companies are not eligible. Work must focus specifically on one of the Trust's priority groups.

grants.title: Our £1m Warm Fund
grants.summary: Year-round support distributed through charity partners to help people most in need keep warm and well at home, including energy efficiency bundles and warm items.
grants.body: The Warm Fund is distributed by the Cadent Foundation's charity partners rather than applied for directly from the Foundation. Support includes bundles for energy efficiency and warm items for use at home. The Cadent Foundation works with charitable organisations to help households improve financial wellbeing and energy efficiency through advice and practical measures. It is a donor advised fund, and grants are administered by Charities Trust.

grants.title: Medium Grants
grants.summary: Grants for urgent and essential fabric repairs to church buildings, such as roof and stone repairs, where the works cost no more than £80,000 including VAT and fees, plus funding for project development work.
grants.body: Medium Grants support urgent and essential repair and maintenance work to listed and other church buildings, including roof work and stone repairs. The works must cost no more than £80,000 including VAT and fees. The scheme also funds investigative and development work centred on an existing church building, such as a structural report or feasibility study, to prepare a stronger proposal for a major grant funder. The Trust does not fund church-based activities, conservation of contents such as artworks, bells or pews, work in churchyards, work to buildings separate from the main church, heating, lighting or reseating alone, new buildings, or buildings no longer used for regular public worship.
grants.eligibility: Churches, chapels and meeting houses with urgent fabric repair needs. Buildings must still be used for regular public worship and must be at least 30 years old, and must have been originally built as a place of worship. Buildings separate from the main church, such as a detached hall, are excluded. Work in churchyards and boundary walls is not funded.

grants.title: Large Grants
grants.summary: Grants for large urgent structural repair projects to church buildings costing over £80,000, and for installing or upgrading kitchens and toilets costing over £30,000.
grants.body: Large Grants fund urgent structural repair projects to church buildings where the work costs more than £80,000 including VAT and fees, such as reroofing, tower or spire work, and stone and masonry repairs. The scheme also funds projects to install or improve kitchen and accessible toilet facilities in a church, where the works cost more than £30,000 including VAT and fees. This can be an extension to the church or a hall connected to the church building. The same exclusions apply as for other Trust grants, including church-based activities, contents, churchyard work, new buildings and buildings no longer used for worship.
grants.eligibility: Churches and places of worship with large urgent structural repair needs, or with kitchen or toilet projects costing over £30,000. Buildings must still be used for regular public worship and must be at least 30 years old, and must have been originally built as a place of worship. A separate building from the church is only eligible where Historic England, Cadw, Historic Environment Scotland or the Department for Communities has advised a separate structure is preferred.

grants.title: Leeds Building Society Foundation Small Grants
grants.summary: Grants of up to £2,500 for UK registered charities with a turnover under £500,000 that support people in need of a safe and secure home. Core, project and capital costs can be funded.
grants.body: The Foundation supports people in need of a safe and secure home. Small grants are open to organisations based anywhere in the UK and are flexible, so groups can apply for core, project or capital costs. Applications must meet at least one of the funding priorities: financial stress, security and refuge, or quality and suitability of housing. Applications can also fall under the theme of health and wellbeing support for those experiencing homelessness, if this is part of wraparound support and another priority is also met. Approaches such as Housing First or relationship-based practice are welcomed. The application window for the December 2026 meeting closed on 11 November 2026.
grants.eligibility: Must be a UK registered charity with a turnover of under £500,000. Organisations can be based anywhere in the UK. The work must support people in need of a safe and secure home.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the grant giving guide before applying. Questions can be sent by email to foundation@leedsbuildingsociety.co.uk.

grants.title: Veolia Environmental Trust grants
grants.summary: Grants towards projects that improve community facilities and the natural environment. Applicants must first check that their project site is in an area the Trust funds.
grants.body: The Trust awards grants for projects that improve community facilities and the natural environment. Before applying, groups need to check that their project site is in an area the Trust funds, using the eligibility checker on the funder's website. The application is worked through in sequence across the funder's eligibility checker, funding criteria and closing dates sections. Details of what can be funded, how much can be requested and the current funding round closing dates are set out on the funder's pages.
grants.eligibility: Projects must take place at a site in an area the Trust funds. Check the eligibility checker before applying.
grants.how_to_apply: Work through the eligibility checker, the funding criteria and the when to apply section in sequence, then apply online through the funder's application portal.

grants.title: Community Buildings
grants.summary: Funds improvements to community buildings such as village halls, community centres and church halls, with grants of £10,000 to £75,000 for eligible projects in England.
grants.body: The theme supports improvements to community buildings used by many groups regularly each week, benefitting a range of people of different ages and backgrounds. Priority is given to projects that show wider community benefit and need. Eligible work includes community room renovations, toilet and kitchen improvements, replacement doors, windows and flooring, failing roofs, extensions to create more community space and new heating systems. Places of worship can apply if the building is used by many wider groups regularly each week, but general building repairs, church windows, spires, steeples and bell towers are not funded. Sporting clubhouses should apply under the Recreation theme. Total project costs or phases must be no more than £200,000 including VAT. Matched funding of at least 10% from a third party contributor is required, the site must be within set distances of a Biffa operation or landfill site, and no more than two full applications per organisation can be made each financial year.
grants.eligibility: Organisations must be fully constituted, charitable or not-for-profit, with no share capital. Local authorities, councils, hospices, hospitals, day-care centres, activity centres, rehabilitation units, residential care facilities, allotments, nurseries, food banks, schools and colleges cannot apply. The site must be open to the public for at least 104 days each year. Work must not have started. If the group does not own the site, it needs a signed lease with at least 10 years remaining. Projects in Scotland and Wales are not accepted.
grants.how_to_apply: Check the site postcode with the Eligibility Checker. If the site is eligible, read the Guidance Notes, then register on the online grants portal to submit an Expression of Interest. Planning permission must be approved before submitting an Expression of Interest.

grants.title: Nature Recovery
grants.summary: Funds projects that protect and restore nature, such as habitat improvement, wetland creation, peatland restoration and tree planting. Grants range from £10,000 to £75,000 for projects that are near an eligible Biffa landfill site.
grants.body: The Nature Recovery theme supports projects that improve habitats, support plants and animals, and help the natural environment respond to challenges such as climate change. Examples include wetland creation, peatland restoration, planting trees, hedgerows and seeds, woodland improvements, wildfire firebreaks, and river or stream work to manage water flow. Staff day rate costs for direct delivery or supervising volunteers can be included where this offers better value than contractors. Research projects, baseline surveys and habitat work on land where the applicant plans to sell biodiversity units are not funded. Projects must have a strong public access or community involvement element, such as volunteering, and must not have already started. The total project cost must be no more than £200,000 including VAT, and a Third Party Contributor must provide 10% of the amount applied for. Applicants can submit up to two full applications per financial year. The site must be within a set distance of an eligible Biffa landfill site or operation and also within 10 miles of a licensed landfill site, which can be checked with the eligibility checker. Applications from Scotland and Wales are no longer accepted.
grants.eligibility: Organisations must be fully constituted, charitable or not-for-profit, and have no share capital. Local authorities, councils, nurseries, food banks, hospices, hospitals, day-care centres, rehabilitation units, residential care facilities, allotments, schools and colleges cannot apply, and projects on those grounds are not funded. The project site must be close to an eligible Biffa landfill site and within 10 miles of a licensed landfill site. If the organisation does not own the site, it needs a signed lease or landowner agreement with at least 10 years remaining. Projects must have secured at least 75% of any shortfall funding and have support from key agencies.
grants.how_to_apply: If the site is eligible, read the Guidance Notes. Register on the online grants portal and submit an Expression of Interest. Access the application later through the Live Projects tab.

grants.title: Biffa Award Recreation theme
grants.summary: Funds improvements that benefit people in their free time, such as accessible play areas, outdoor gyms, nature trails, woodland walks and wheeled sports ramps. Grants are between £10,000 and £75,000.
grants.body: The Recreation theme supports projects that improve facilities people use in their free time, including fixed play equipment and outdoor gyms, fixed ramps for wheeled sports, plants and seed for woodland walks and nature trails, and community room, toilet and kitchen improvements in a clubhouse. Priority goes to projects with wider community benefit that are used by many people each week across different ages and backgrounds. Projects must cost no more than £200,000 including VAT, the site must be open to the public for at least 104 days a year, and the work must not have started. The site must be within 5 miles of an eligible Biffa operation or 10 miles of a Biffa landfill site, and within 10 miles of a licensed landfill site. A third party contribution of 10% of the amount applied for is required, along with at least 75% of any shortfall funding secured. Organisations can submit up to two Full Applications each financial year, and a project must fit under one funding theme only. Applications from Scotland and Wales are no longer accepted.
grants.eligibility: Applicants must be fully constituted, charitable or not-for-profit, with no share capital. Local authorities, councils, hospices, hospitals, day-care centres, activity centres, rehabilitation units, residential care facilities, allotments, nurseries, food banks, schools and colleges cannot apply. Sporting clubhouse projects are only considered for internal renovation where the space serves the wider community like a village hall. Changing rooms, showers, toilets, sports kits, pitch repairs, courts, greens, nets, external lighting and drainage cannot be funded. Sites must be publicly available, and a lease of at least 10 years remaining is needed if the organisation does not own the site.
grants.how_to_apply: If eligible, read the Guidance Notes and register on the online grants portal to submit an Expression of Interest. Planning permission must be approved before the Expression of Interest is submitted.

grants.title: Group grants for small community groups and local charities
grants.summary: Grants of £100 to £2,600 for activities, outings, equipment and materials for members or service users of small community groups and local charities. Group applications reopen on 4 January 2027.
grants.body: The foundation supports projects that connect or reconnect people with others in their local community, combating isolation and loneliness and enabling older people and adults with disabilities to be active and engaged. The group programme helps with activities, outings, equipment and materials for members or service users. Applicants should have a cost breakdown or budget ready, along with their latest annual accounts to upload. Group applications are open in January, April, July and October, with outcomes notified within two months. The group round is currently closed and is due to reopen on 4 January.
grants.eligibility: Small community groups and small local charities working with older people and other adults with a disability or mental health condition. Individuals cannot apply to this group programme.
grants.how_to_apply: Prepare a cost breakdown or budget and your latest annual accounts for upload. Complete the online application in one of the quarterly windows, which are January, April, July and October. Outcomes are notified within two months.

grants.title: Main and Small Fund
grants.summary: Funds energy-specific projects that support energy consumers in vulnerable situations and help people most at risk from cold homes and high energy bills. Small Fund grants are £20,000 to £50,000 and Main Fund grants start at £50,000.
grants.body: This fund supports energy advice and support, installation of energy saving or renewable energy measures, training and education on energy issues, and crisis support linked to energy bills or property energy efficiency, but only as part of a wider energy advice project. Projects expected to cost under £50,000 should apply to the Small Fund, and projects costing over £50,000 should apply to the Main Fund. Grants can cover up to 100% of project costs over up to 2 years. Advice on benefits, income, debt or housing that is not energy specific cannot be funded, and energy saving measures that other schemes such as the Energy Company Obligation can fund are excluded.
grants.eligibility: Charities and community energy groups can apply. Projects must deliver energy related work for energy consumers in vulnerable situations across England, Scotland and Wales.
grants.how_to_apply: Register your organisation at least 2 weeks before a funding round deadline, read the guidance, prepare your application and apply in one of the quarterly rounds.

grants.title: Impact Fund
grants.summary: Funds projects that pilot robust monitoring to measure the impact of fuel poverty support for energy consumers in vulnerable situations. Grants start at £20,000 and cover up to 100% of costs over up to 2 years.
grants.body: The Impact Fund pays for collecting and analysing data on which interventions reduce fuel poverty, monitoring equipment, evaluation, specialist support to evidence impact, and fuel poverty advice that is monitored for impact. Projects must collect robust information on tangible benefits to energy consumers, use this to learn lessons, and share good practice with the wider fuel poverty sector. Projects must have a robust plan to measure impact and a clear plan to contribute learning. Monitoring that extends beyond the grant period cannot be funded, as redress funding is limited to 24 months.
grants.eligibility: Charities and community energy groups can apply. Projects must focus on supporting energy consumers in vulnerable situations across England, Scotland and Wales.
grants.how_to_apply: Register your organisation at least 2 weeks before a funding round deadline, read the Impact Fund guidance, prepare your application and apply in one of the quarterly rounds.

grants.title: Innovation Fund
grants.summary: Funds innovative energy products and services that benefit energy consumers and reduce the environmental impact of energy use. Grants start at £20,000 and cover up to 100% of costs over up to 2 years.
grants.body: The fund supports research and analysis into product or service development, and trials of products or services that are ready to implement but not yet accessible to energy consumers or certain groups of consumers. Projects must have a realistic prospect of benefiting existing or future energy consumers and must help reduce the environmental impact of energy use. Projects must show genuine innovation, testing, research or development. Up to 15 percent of Energy Redress funds can support innovation projects.
grants.eligibility: Charities and community energy groups can apply. Projects must benefit energy consumers across England, Scotland and Wales.
grants.how_to_apply: Register your organisation at least 2 weeks before a funding round deadline, read the guidance, prepare your application and apply in one of the quarterly rounds.

grants.title: Carbon Emissions Reduction Fund (CERF)
grants.summary: Funds energy related activity that reduces carbon dioxide emissions from energy generation, distribution or use, such as community energy and low-carbon access projects. Grants start at £20,000 and cover up to 100% of costs over up to 2 years.
grants.body: Eligible activity includes community energy projects, including collective ownership of renewable energy assets, improving household and community access to low-carbon technologies, strengthening local supply chains, and collective purchasing schemes that make efficiency and renewable measures more affordable. Projects must show measurable and lasting reductions in carbon intensity of energy use and a realistic prospect of broadly replicable benefits. Awareness-raising projects without a clear route to carbon reductions are excluded, as are tree planting, carbon offsetting, transport and waste projects. Up to 15 percent of Energy Redress funds can support carbon reduction activity.
grants.eligibility: Charities and community energy groups can apply. Projects must be energy related and within Ofgem's regulatory remit, across England, Scotland and Wales.
grants.how_to_apply: Register your organisation at least 2 weeks before a funding round deadline, read the guidance, prepare your application and apply in one of the quarterly rounds.

grants.title: Just Transition Fund
grants.summary: Funds development work for community-led renewable energy projects that bring benefits to energy consumers in vulnerable situations. Grants start at £20,000 and cover up to 100% of costs over up to 2 years.
grants.body: The fund pays for development work for community renewable energy schemes, including staff time and specialist support such as feasibility studies, business modelling, surveys and planning, along with engagement and consultation costs that help projects reach investment readiness. Projects must bring tangible benefits to energy consumers in vulnerable situations, for example by using energy sales profits to create local fuel poverty funds or providing affordable energy directly. Capital costs and installation or construction costs are excluded. Funding rounds are announced quarterly, and some rounds may add specific priorities that are set out when the round opens.
grants.eligibility: Charities and community energy groups can apply. Projects must bring benefits to energy consumers in vulnerable situations across England, Scotland and Wales. Capital and installation costs cannot be funded.
grants.how_to_apply: Register your organisation at least 2 weeks before a funding round deadline, read the guidance, prepare your application and apply in one of the quarterly rounds.

sources.name: FCC Communities Foundation: Community Action Fund

grants.title: FCC Community Action Fund
grants.summary: Grants of £10,000 to £100,000 for not-for-profit amenity projects eligible under Object D and Object DA of the Landfill Communities Fund, sited within 10 miles of an eligible FCC Environment waste facility.
grants.body: The fund supports amenity projects that qualify under Object D and Object DA of the Landfill Communities Fund. Projects must be sited within 10 miles of an eligible FCC Environment waste facility, and applicants can check eligibility through a pre-application check. The fund is oversubscribed and limits the types of project it will support and the costs it will pay for. Applicants should read the current Guide for Applicants before applying. The 2027-1 round opens on 25 November 2026 and closes at 5.00pm on 24 February 2027. Board decisions are made quarterly, about three months after each round closes.
grants.eligibility: Open to not-for-profit organisations. Projects must be sited within 10 miles of an eligible FCC Environment waste facility.
grants.how_to_apply: Complete the pre-application eligibility check through the Apply link. Read the Guide for Applicants before submitting an application in the funding round.

grants.title: SUEZ Communities Fund - England
grants.summary: Grants for projects in communities near SUEZ operational sites in England, funded through the Landfill Communities Fund. Projects must be within an active funding zone checked by postcode.
grants.body: The fund uses donations from SUEZ Recycling and Recovery UK through the Landfill Communities Fund, and covers projects located within one of the company's active funding zones in England. A funding zone is the area surrounding a qualifying SUEZ site. The fund has been extended to include a number of SUEZ operational sites in Lancashire from 7 May 2026. Applicants must confirm their project location with the Postcode Checker before applying. Projects must have secured all required consents, such as planning permission, and any other funding needed for the project to proceed. Applications for consent that have not yet been approved are not accepted. There are normally four funding rounds a year and applications must be made through the online form. Applications received after a closing date move to the next round if one is available.
grants.eligibility: Organisations must have a project located within an active SUEZ funding zone in England, confirmed through the Postcode Checker. All required consents and other necessary funding must be secured before applying.
grants.how_to_apply: Check your project location with the Postcode Checker, then complete the online application form. Applications in other formats are not accepted. Decisions for the 18 November 2026 round are expected in early February 2027.

sources.name: Point North: Hook Moor Wind Farm Community Fund

grants.title: Hook Moor Wind Farm Community Fund
grants.summary: Grants of up to £3,000 for community groups, voluntary organisations and environmental projects in the parishes of Aberford and Micklefield, near Hook Moor Wind Farm. Applications close 22 November 2026.
grants.body: The fund supports local community groups, voluntary organisations and environmental projects that fight poverty and enrich lives in the communities around Hook Moor Wind Farm. It covers projects such as energy efficiency, environmental protection and nature conservation, health and wellbeing activities, regeneration, improvements to community facilities, education and training equipment, and social welfare activities such as lunch clubs, food banks, trips and events. The fund does not pay for salaries, religious advancement, political activity, activities that are the responsibility of statutory authorities, or costs incurred before a grant is formally approved. Projects must benefit the Aberford and Micklefield area, although projects outside it may be considered if they clearly benefit local people from those places. A registered charity is not required, but applicants must have charitable aims. Decisions are aimed to be made within 12 weeks of a complete application.
grants.eligibility: Community groups, voluntary organisations and other groups with charitable aims serving Aberford or Micklefield in West Yorkshire. Registered charity status is not required. Projects outside these parishes may be considered if they benefit local people from them. Salaries and religious or political activity are not eligible.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the application guidelines in full and check you meet the eligibility criteria. Complete the online application form through the application portal. The aim is to give a decision within 12 weeks of a completed application.

grants.title: Community Builders Fund
grants.summary: A loan fund from Social Investment Business for charities and social enterprises in the UK, with loans from £100,000 to £1,500,000.
grants.body: The Community Builders Fund offers loans to charities and social enterprises to help them grow and deliver their services. The loan range is £100,000 to £1,500,000.

grants.title: Energy Resilience Fund
grants.summary: A grant and loan fund for organisations in England to improve their energy resilience, with funding from £25,000 to £500,000 including a 40% grant element.
grants.body: The Energy Resilience Fund combines grants and loans to help organisations in England become more resilient to rising energy costs and improve how they use energy. Funding ranges from £25,000 to £500,000.

grants.title: Reach Fund
grants.summary: A grant fund for charities and social enterprises in England, with grants from £5,000 to £15,000.
grants.body: The Reach Fund provides grants to charities and social enterprises in England. Grants range from £5,000 to £15,000.

grants.title: Flexible Finance Fund
grants.summary: A blend of loan and unrestricted grant for Black and Racially Minoritised led charities and social enterprises in England. Loans range from £50,000 to £1.5 million, with a grant of 50% to 100% of the loan capped at £200,000.
grants.body: The Flexible Finance Fund provides a package of loan and grant funding, plus support, to help eligible organisations grow, take on assets and become more resilient. It is delivered by Social Investment Business with The Ubele Initiative and Create Equity, and the loan element is backed by the Government's Growth Guarantee Scheme. The loan can be used for any purpose, and the grant element is unrestricted but cannot be used for refinancing. Loans of up to £250,000 are unsecured, with repayment terms of 1 to 6 years, a fixed interest rate of 7.9% and an arrangement fee of 2.5% or 3%. A restricted support grant of up to £15,000 is also available to blended loan and grant customers to address identified areas of weakness. The assistance may be regarded as a subsidy. Applicants should check the eligibility criteria and the Application Form Guidance before applying, and the funder offers help with eligibility questions by email.
grants.eligibility: Organisations must be based in England and be Black and Racially Minoritised led, with 51% or more of the board and senior management team from Black and Racially Minoritised backgrounds. They must be legally constituted and a registered charity or social enterprise, including a charity, community interest company or community benefit society, or comply with the BSC Governance Principles. The organisation must be primarily constituted for social benefit within England and have operated for at least two years, with a minimum turnover of £200,000 in the last financial year. Organisations must not be in insolvency proceedings and must not have received repayable finance over £25,000, excluding Bounce Back Loans.
grants.how_to_apply: Submit an application online. The funder contacts applicants with any questions, the application then goes to the committee, and the funder confirms its decision.

grants.title: Northern Impact Fund 2
grants.summary: Investments from £5,000 to £150,000 to support trading growth, including cash flow, working capital, and asset development or purchase, for social enterprises and charitable organisations in the North of England.
grants.body: The fund supports the development or growth of trading activity. It can be used for cash flow, working capital, and asset development or purchase. Investments run for 1 to 5 years. Key Fund says its investment team will help you identify the right type of funding, support you through the application and provide aftercare.
grants.eligibility: Social enterprises, charitable organisations and small businesses based in the North of England or Midlands, or intending to form a legal company. The organisation must have a direct social mission at its heart and must have been declined by a mainstream bank.
grants.how_to_apply: Select Apply on the fund page. Key Fund's investment team will work with you through the application process. You can call Key Fund on 0330 202 0559 with questions.

grants.title: Regional Growth Fund
grants.summary: Investments of up to £150,000 for enterprises in disadvantaged areas or serving disadvantaged groups, with Key Fund targeting social and community organisations. Terms run up to 7 years at a usual flat rate of 8.25%.
grants.body: The fund supports the development and growth of economic activity and employment in disadvantaged areas or for disadvantaged groups, by investing in enterprises. The fund is not limited to social or community organisations, although Key Fund will target these organisations. Terms run up to 7 years, with interest usually charged at a flat rate of 8.25%.
grants.eligibility: Enterprises operating in disadvantaged areas or serving disadvantaged groups. Social and community organisations are targeted, but the fund is not restricted to them.
grants.how_to_apply: Select Apply on the fund page. Key Fund's investment team will guide you through the application process.

grants.body: The fund supports social enterprises that have been trading for over 1 year and want to purchase or develop properties. Investments are available up to £300,000 with terms of up to 10 years and a 4.5% flat interest rate.
grants.eligibility: Social enterprises in the Yorkshire and Humber region that are over 1 year old and looking to purchase or develop properties.
grants.how_to_apply: Select Apply on the fund page. Key Fund's investment team will support you through the application process.

grants.title: The DPS Social Commitment Programme: Activate
grants.funder: The Deposit Protection Service (The DPS), funded through Computershare Investor Services PLC, delivered with School for Social Entrepreneurs (SSE)
grants.summary: A nine-month accelerator learning programme with grant funding for early-stage charities and social enterprises in England and Wales working to help people find and keep a stable home and reduce homelessness.
grants.body: The programme supports early-stage organisations whose business model has been piloted and needs help to develop further and reach market. It combines a specialist learning programme, expert advice, coaching and mentoring, peer-to-peer learning and a ready-made network of others working on housing insecurity. Grant funding is up to £7,000 or £10,000 depending on the level. Activate is for organisations likely to have annual income under £100,000. The programme runs from 1 April 2027 to 1 December 2027 and takes up to a year, with 12 sessions, 1:1 support and a market making event.
grants.eligibility: Organisations based in England or Wales broadly working on issues that affect a person's ability to find and sustain a stable home. Intended for early-stage organisations likely to have annual income under £100,000 in the last financial year, counting grants, donations and trading income but not loans or equity.
grants.how_to_apply: Choose the Activate programme on the SSE website and register interest on its programme page. Registered applicants receive information, guidance notes and a link to the online application form, and can attend an optional info session. Apply through the online form before the deadline of 16 November 2026 at 12pm.

grants.title: Mayor's Safer Communities Fund
grants.summary: Grants for projects that prevent crime and make communities safer across West Yorkshire, delivered within 12 months.
grants.body: The fund supports community projects that help keep people safe and reduce crime in West Yorkshire. Projects must take place within West Yorkshire and must be spent within 12 months of allocation. The fund will not support private companies, general appeals, projects longer than 12 months, projects outside West Yorkshire, pure academic research, bursaries, individuals, work that is a statutory requirement, food for foodbanks, refreshments, the replacement of statutory funding, or retrospective grants. Long term capital projects are not eligible. Transport costs can be included only if they are within West Yorkshire and part of a wider project. A project that covers more than one district must be submitted as a single application. A group can only reapply once it has returned a satisfactory evaluation and finance form for earlier funding.
grants.eligibility: Open to voluntary and community groups, charities and not-for-profit groups, as well as West Yorkshire local authorities and statutory agencies. Applicants must deliver projects in West Yorkshire. Individuals, private companies and projects that are a statutory duty are excluded. Successful applicants to The People's Fund, awarded June 2026, are eligible to apply to this round.

grants.title: Wellbeing Fund
grants.summary: Community committee grants for large projects supporting the social, economic and environmental wellbeing of a committee area in Leeds. Grants over £1,000 per ward.
grants.body: Each of the eight Leeds community committees is allocated a budget at the start of each year, which it awards as grants to community projects that meet local priorities agreed by the committee. The Wellbeing Fund covers larger projects that support the social, economic and environmental wellbeing of the committee area. Small grants of up to £1,000 per ward and large grants over £1,000 per ward are available. Committees make decisions at public meetings held four times a year, in line with their forward plan and finance report. For eligibility or to check whether a project fits, contact the community committee support team.
grants.eligibility: Open to voluntary, community or faith organisations, charities, commercial organisations operating on a non-profit basis and council services. Projects must benefit the local committee area.
grants.how_to_apply: Contact the community committee support team to confirm eligibility. Applications are considered by the relevant community committee at its public meetings.

grants.title: Youth Activity Fund
grants.summary: Community committee grants for activities for children and young people aged 8 to 17 in each committee area of Leeds. Grants up to £1,000 per ward for small grants.
grants.body: Each community committee in Leeds is allocated a youth activities fund at the start of each year, awarded as grants to youth activities that meet local priorities. The Youth Activity Fund provides activities for children and young people aged 8 to 17 in the committee area. Small grants of up to £1,000 per ward and large grants over £1,000 per ward are available. Decisions are made by elected members at public community committee meetings. To check eligibility, contact the community committee support team.
grants.eligibility: Open to voluntary, community or faith organisations, charities, commercial organisations operating on a non-profit basis and council services. Activities must be for children and young people aged 8 to 17 in the committee area.
grants.how_to_apply: Contact the community committee support team or your local elected members to discuss an application. Applications are considered at public community committee meetings.

grants.title: Local Community Fund
grants.summary: Co-op members choose local causes to receive a share of Co-op profits. The fund supports projects that give people access to opportunities and resources in their communities.
grants.body: The Local Community Fund supports projects in members' communities that provide access to opportunities and resources for people to thrive. Co-op Members choose which local cause they want to support through the Co-op App or their membership account, and the Co-op shares profits with the chosen causes.
grants.how_to_apply: Co-op Members choose a local cause to support by signing into their online membership account or by using the Co-op App and selecting a cause under the Wallet tab.

grants.title: Trading for Good
grants.summary: A specialist support programme for community businesses to develop trading income, including a Match Trading Grant and a learning programme.
grants.body: Trading for Good supports community businesses to develop their trading income streams and build a more resilient organisation. It combines a specialist programme of support with a learning programme. The programme includes a Match Trading Grant. Community businesses taking part can use it to develop their trading activity.

grants.title: Community Champions
grants.summary: Persimmon's local offices make quarterly donations of up to £6,000 to local charities, sports clubs and good causes, with smaller donations also available.
grants.body: Each of Persimmon's 30 UK offices makes donations of up to £6,000 every quarter to local organisations. The scheme supports local charities, sports clubs and good causes in the communities where Persimmon builds homes. Smaller donations are also available. Applications are made through an online form stating why the group deserves support and how much is sought. The group must also give its location and contact details so the application can be passed to the relevant local Persimmon office.
grants.eligibility: Local charities, sports clubs and good causes in areas where Persimmon has offices.
grants.how_to_apply: Complete the online donation form, explaining why your group deserves support and how much you are seeking, with your location and contact information. Applications are passed to the relevant local office.

grants.title: Community Impact Grants
grants.summary: Revenue funding for Christian-led community projects that address social challenges or grow congregations and Christian communities across the UK and Ireland.
grants.body: The programme supports projects that address social challenges such as poverty, homelessness, isolation and loneliness, and addiction or substance misuse. It also supports work that grows and sustains congregations, including faith development, youth work, church planting, volunteer training, and staff roles that support long-term sustainability. Projects typically run for up to three years. Core costs may be included where they are essential to delivering the project. The programme does not fund capital or building work; church repairs, restoration and building projects should go to the Building Grants programme. Schools and hospices are not eligible for this programme but can apply to Building Grants for chapel projects. Read the programme guidance before applying to check eligibility and fit.
grants.eligibility: Open to Christian charities, churches and cathedrals, and dioceses and denominational bodies delivering community-focused projects. Schools and hospices are not eligible. Funding supports community activity and service delivery rather than building or construction work.
grants.how_to_apply: Read the Community Impact Grants programme guidance before submitting an application.
